pages.observed: Five samples 0.0 to 0.8 s of a curbside airport pickup scene. A phone card reads Ride requested over a route map, a white sensor-roofed car sits at the far left edge, an empty marked pickup bay is at center, and the lower half is empty dark roadway. Caption Anyone in San Antonio can now hail a Waymo with no driver, appears from 0.6 s.

1.0 to 1.8 s. The white sensor-roofed car has entered from the left and by 1.2 s sits inside the marked bay with its red brake lamp lit; it then holds in place. Phone card still reads Ride requested. Caption stays on the upper road just below the car wheels. Lower 40 percent of frame is empty dark road.

2.0 to 2.8 s. Car holds in the bay, then at about 2.4 s the picture cuts inside the cab, viewed from behind the front seats: steering wheel, center map screen, empty headrests, windshield with the airport sign moving across. A small Texas outline card appears top right from 2.2 s. Steering wheel rotation is not clearly visible in these samples. Caption sits over the seat backs.

3.0 to 3.8 s cab interior. The tan marker on the steering wheel rim moves from upper right to the right side, so the wheel turns with no hands present. The windshield is largely an empty pale field as the airport sign slides out right. The Texas outline is drawn into the locator card. Seat backs fill the lower half under the caption.

4.0 to 4.6 s the cab interior holds with the wheel marker parked on the right side and a mostly blank windshield. Caption clears at 4.6 s. At 4.8 s a new shot shows the curb with an enlarged tilted phone reading Ride requested, Finding a car in front of a small white car at the bay. Bottom 40 percent of the 4.8 s frame is a flat grey band and dark empty road.

5.0 to 5.8 s. The phone dominates the left of the frame and its car marker slides to the pin; the status text changes from Ride requested to Arriving, At the curb at 5.6 s. The parked white car beside the airport sign stays still. Caption reads the airport included. A ring appears on the Texas locator. Bottom 40 percent is empty grey and dark road.

6.0 to 6.6 s the curb shot holds still with the phone at Arriving and the car parked; the caption ends at 6.0 s. At 6.8 s the picture cuts to a pale paper map lying on a brown wooden table with a February calendar card standing at its top edge; the map shows only a faint grid, three small pin marks and two faint green patches. The car pin crossing from curb to map is not visible.

7.0 to 7.8 s. A small pale paper map sits on a brown table with a February calendar card at its top right. Until 7.4 s it shows only a faint grid and three small pins. From 7.6 s a blue river line and thin orange street lines start drawing on it. The map is small in frame with large empty sky above and table below. Caption reads The service began in February.

8.0 to 8.8 s. On the small table map the blue river line and an orange ring road with radiating orange roads finish drawing, then hold. Three small pins sit near the center. The February card stays at top right. The Texas locator fades away at 8.0 s. No limited-area outline or size tag is visible yet. Large empty sky and table fill above and below.

9.0 to 9.8 s. The view moves closer so the map fills the upper two thirds. The February calendar card tilts and travels across the map from the right to the lower left. A thin black outline starts tracing at the top of the ring road, reaching a short bent line by 9.8 s. Caption changes at 9.4 s to in a limited area of sixty square miles.

10.0 to 10.8 s. The enlarged map holds with the February card settled at its lower left. The black outline covers only the upper arc of the ring road and grows by one short segment at 10.8 s. No closed area and no sixty square miles tag are visible on the map in these samples. Caption reads in a limited area of sixty square miles.

11.0 to 11.8 s. The black outline traces around the right and bottom of the map and closes into a polygon by 11.4 s, which fills light grey and encloses the three pins. A pinned paper tag reading 60 square miles, Limited area drops in at 11.2 s and settles flat at the map top right. The completed result holds through 11.8 s.

12.0 to 12.2 s the completed map holds without a caption. At 12.4 s it cuts to a wide brown water scene with a small white sensor-roofed car sitting in the water mid-frame, a stepped pale limestone bank at right, live oaks and a distant skyline. The disclosure now reads A different car, April 20th account. No rain streaks are visible and the car does not move across 12.4 to 12.8 s. The car occupies a small fraction of the frame.

13.0 to 13.8 s. Static wide creek shot: the small white car sits half submerged in brown water with its reflection, limestone ledges at right, trees and skyline beyond. Thin faint rain streaks are visible over the lower water. The car does not change position or orientation across these samples. Cabin interior is not readable at this size. The caption box sits immediately under the car.

14.0 to 14.6 s the wide creek view holds with the car stationary and faint rain on the water. At 14.8 s the picture cuts to a closer view: the white car sits broadside in brown water up to mid-door, windows showing an empty cabin, with small ripple lines at its nose and tail. Caption box stays under the car.

15.0 to 15.8 s medium creek shot. The white car sits broadside in brown water up to mid-door, seats visible through the windows with nobody inside, a pale bow wave at its right end and rain streaks on the water. It stays in nearly the same place through 15.6 s; at 15.8 s the body is tilted a few degrees. No sideways lift or downstream travel is visible in these samples.

16.0 to 16.8 s. The white car is now lifted and tilted with both wheels showing above the brown water, a mud band on its lower doors and an empty cabin. It drifts steadily leftward across the frame with a curved wake and splash trailing on its right. Rain streaks continue on the water. The caption remains just under the car.

17.0 to 17.2 s the swept creek car holds tilted at the left edge with no caption. At 17.4 s the picture cuts to a residential street: tan house, live oak, fence and green street sign behind; a small white car on dark asphalt with brown floodwater spreading from the left to around its rear wheel. The bottom third is plain pale sidewalk. Disclosure reads Another car, earlier in April.

18.0 to 18.8 s. Brown floodwater spreads rightward until it covers the whole street by 18.4 s, then rises from the wheel bottoms to above the wheel arches by 18.6 s. The small white car sits in it, moving slightly right early then holding. House, live oak and street sign behind; plain pale sidewalk occupies the bottom third. No hazard lamp blinking is distinguishable at this size.

19.0 to 19.8 s. The small white car sits stopped in brown floodwater above its wheel arches. A small amber lamp glow appears at its front corner at 19.2 and 19.4 s and is gone at 19.6 s, consistent with blinking. At 19.8 s the view changes to a closer framing with the car larger, the background softened, and empty seats visible through the windows.

20.0 to 20.8 s closer street-flood shot. The white car sits stopped in brown floodwater above its wheel arches with empty seats visible through the windows. Amber hazard glows appear at its front and rear corners and change between samples, consistent with blinking. The water holds flat around the car. Background is softened; the caption sits at the curb line below the car.

21.0 to 21.8 s. The same closer street-flood shot holds: the empty white car stopped in floodwater, amber hazard lamps alternating bright and dim at front and rear across the samples. The caption ends after 21.2 s and the shot holds without text to 21.8 s.

22.0 s ends the street flood. At 22.2 s the picture cuts to an olive wall over a brown desk where a tilted cream card headed Federal recall record, Vehicle safety recall slides in from the right and settles by 22.8 s. Its ruled rows are still blank and a dark pen rests at its lower corner. The bottom 20 percent is a flat olive band. Caption Waymo filed a software recall appears at 22.6 s.

23.0 to 23.8 s. The recall card slides left and squares up on the desk while its rows write in: Recall type Software, Potential units affected 3,791, then a Summary reading The software may allow the vehicle to slow and then drive into standing water on higher speed roadways. Row labels are very small at phone size; the 3,791 figure overlaps its label. A pen lies beside the card without moving.

24.0 to 24.6 s the recall card keeps writing rows: Remedy, The remedy is currently under development; Interim remedy, Weather-related constraints increased, Vehicle maps updated; Interim update, All affected vehicles by April 20th, 2026. Text is small at phone size. At 24.8 s the view cuts overhead to a smaller card at top and a grid of dashed empty car outlines with four filled white car icons. Caption changes to that could affect nearly thirty eight hundred cars.

25.0 to 25.8 s overhead desk. The 10 by 8 grid of small white car icons fills row by row until complete at 25.8 s. A hand and forearm holding a wooden stamp descend from the top right edge and reach the top of the recall card by 25.8 s. The card's rows are too small to read at phone size. No counter tag is visible yet.

26.0 to 26.8 s. A forearm and hand press a wooden stamp onto the top of the recall card; as it lifts away an amber Software recall mark remains. A pinned counter tag fades in at 26.2 s reading Nearly 3,800 vehicles, 3,791 potentially affected in the record, overlapping the card's left edge. The full grid of 80 car icons holds below. Stamp mark text is small at phone size.

27.0 to 27.8 s. Static hold on the completed overhead desk: the pinned Nearly 3,800 vehicles, 3,791 potentially affected in the record tag, the stamped recall card and the full grid of car icons. The caption clears after 27.4 s. Nothing moves in these samples.

28.0 s is the last recall desk frame. At 28.2 s the picture cuts to a wide road: a white sensor-roofed car enters from the left on a dark lane with dashed markings, a lamp post, trees and skyline behind, green verge filling the lower 40 percent. By 28.8 s the car is fully in frame moving right, and a quote card reading The software may allow the vehicle to slow and then drive into standing water on higher speed roadways fades in at upper left. No water is visible on the lane yet.

29.0 to 29.8 s. The white car travels the lane with the view tracking it: the car stays near left-center while dashes and the lamp post slide away left. The recall quote card stays at upper left. No standing water and no lit brake lamp are visible yet. Caption The recall says the software may let a car slow sits just under the car.

30.0 to 30.8 s. The car's red brake lamp is lit while a grey-blue standing-water patch slides in from the right edge of the lane toward it. The water patch is partly covered at its lower edge by the caption box. The car is still on dry pavement short of the water at 30.8 s. Quote card stays at upper left.

31.0 to 31.4 s the small car nears the grey-blue water patch on the wide lane. At 31.6 s the picture cuts to a close side view where the car fills the frame width on dark pavement with a thin white wavy line under its tires; at 31.8 s a water edge only begins to appear at the right frame edge. Caption changes to then drive into standing water on higher speed roads.

32.0 to 32.8 s close side view. The standing-water patch extends from the right edge toward the car and meets its front tire at 32.6 to 32.8 s, where a small splash appears. At 32.8 s the word may in the quote card is highlighted amber. The car holds its screen position as the water arrives under it. Caption reads then drive into standing water on higher speed roads.

33.0 to 33.8 s close side view. The car rolls onto the grey-blue standing water, which spreads under both wheels by 33.4 s, and white wake lines stream from its wheels and lower body while the lane dashes keep scrolling. The word may stays highlighted amber in the quote card. Water depth reads as a shallow sheet at tire level.

34.0 to 34.8 s. The close side view holds the car rolling in the standing water with wake lines at both wheels and a grey splash under the front bumper. The quote card keeps may highlighted. The picture changes little across these samples; a thin vertical post appears at the right edge at 34.8 s.

35.0 to 35.4 s the close lane shot holds with the car in the water and no caption. At 35.6 s the picture cuts to the recall card enlarged on the desk, all rows filled and the amber Software recall stamp across its top rows, which partly covers the units figure. Caption The federal record says the remedy is currently under development appears at 35.8 s.

36.0 to 36.8 s. The enlarged recall card holds on the desk; at 36.2 s its Remedy row lights with a pale amber band reading The remedy is currently under development. At 36.8 s a pen tip enters from the right edge. The lower 40 percent is empty desk and olive band apart from the caption. Row text is small at phone size; the highlighted remedy text is legible.

37.0 to 37.8 s. A hand holding a pen reaches in from the right; the pen tip stops at the card's right margin roughly beside the remedy and interim remedy rows rather than on the remedy text, then withdraws by 37.6 s. At 37.8 s the view is closer and a hand presses a wooden stamp onto the card's upper area over the existing Software recall stamp and part of the Summary row. The remedy row stays highlighted.

38.0 to 38.8 s closer card view. A blue-sleeved forearm from the top right carries a wooden stamp down across the Summary row to the highlighted Remedy row, presses at 38.6 s, and lifts at 38.8 s leaving an amber Under development mark over the remedy text. During the move the arm covers the Software recall stamp and Summary text. The stamp mark partly overlays the words it confirms.

39.0 to 39.8 s. The stamp hand rises and exits the top right edge, leaving the card with two amber marks: Software recall across the top rows and Under development across the remedy row. The Under development mark covers most of the words The remedy is currently under development beneath it. Caption ends after 39.2 s; the card holds.

40.0 to 40.8 s. A wide parking-lot shot: four small white sensor-roofed cars in a row of angled stalls, two poles with a wire overhead, an April calendar card and a small Vehicle maps card hung on the left pole, skyline behind. The cars are small in frame and the lower 45 percent is empty asphalt. No weather limits tag is visible yet. Caption As an interim step, Waymo tightened its weather limits appears at 40.4 s.

41.0 to 41.8 s. In the wide parking-lot shot, a tag with a rain-cloud icon reading Weather limits, tightened slides in from the left at 41.4 s across the April card and settles pinned to the overhead wire near center at 41.8 s. The four small cars in the row below do not change. The tag is small relative to the frame.

42.0 to 42.8 s. The wide parking-lot shot holds unchanged: Weather limits, tightened tag on the wire, April and Vehicle maps cards on the pole, four small cars in the row, empty asphalt in the lower 45 percent. Nothing in the frame moves across these five samples.

43.0 to 43.4 s the parking-lot shot remains unchanged. At 43.6 s the framing shifts slightly closer with the cars a little larger. The April calendar card still shows only blank lines. Caption changes at 43.8 s to and every affected car had the update by April twentieth. No check marks on the cars yet.

44.0 to 44.8 s. The calendar card on the left pole flips: a page lifts up and away above it while the card shows April and a large 20, settled by 44.6 s. The Weather limits tag and Vehicle maps card stay put. The four small cars below show no check marks yet. Lower 45 percent remains empty asphalt.

45.0 to 45.8 s. After a static moment, a small pale dot travels along above the car row; at 45.6 s a round check-mark badge appears over the first car and at 45.8 s over the second. The April 20 calendar, Weather limits tag and Vehicle maps card hold. Badges and cars are small at phone size.

46.0 to 46.8 s. Check-mark badges complete across the row: three at 46.0 s, all four by 46.2 s, when the Vehicle maps card also gains a check mark and an updated label. The completed state then holds with April 20, Weather limits tightened, and the four checked cars. Elements remain small with empty asphalt in the lower 45 percent.

47.0 to 47.6 s the completed parking-lot state holds, caption clearing after 47.0 s. At 47.8 s the picture cuts back to the airport curb: the white sensor-roofed car parked in the bay by the airport sign, the phone card at top left reading Arriving, bench and suitcase behind. Disclosure reads A generic airport ride, not the flood cars. The car's doors are closed in this sample.

48.0 to 48.8 s. Wide airport curb shot matching the opening composition. The white car sits in the bay and its near-side rear door starts to swing open at 48.4 s, clearly open with a dark gap by 48.8 s. The phone card at top left still reads Arriving. Caption So the airport ride is open. Lower 40 percent is empty road.

49.0 to 49.8 s. The wide curb shot holds with the white car's rear door standing open and a beige interior visible. Nobody approaches the car. The phone card still reads Arriving. The caption ends after 49.6 s; the lower 40 percent remains empty road with a dashed lane line.

50.0 to 50.8 s. A medium curb framing shows the white car with its rear door open by the airport sign, a phone propped on the bench, and a small recall card lying on the road surface in the foreground reading The remedy is currently under development with a tiny Under development stamp. The card is already in place at 50.0 s and does not move in these samples. Card text is small at phone size.

51.0 to 51.8 s. The foreground recall card grows and slides toward the left, settling by 51.6 s; its remedy row is highlighted with The remedy is currently under development and an amber Under development stamp, now legible. The card's bottom edge butts against the top of the caption box. The car with its open door stays at the curb behind.

52.0 to 52.8 s. Static hold: open-door car at the curb behind, the recall card at left foreground showing The remedy is currently under development with its amber stamp. The caption briefly clears at 52.6 s and returns at 52.8 s reading as currently under development. No visible motion.

53.0 to 53.8 s. The picture cuts to a split: upper half a closer view of the open-door white car at the curb under the airport sign; lower half a brown desk holding the recall card, with its highlighted remedy row and Under development stamp, beside a phone showing a route and Arriving. A dark underline draws beneath under development by 53.6 s. Caption as currently under development. The lower 30 percent is empty desk.

54.0 to 54.8 s. The split composition holds: open-door car at the airport curb above, recall card with The remedy is currently under development and its stamp beside the Arriving phone on the desk below. The caption ends after 54.0 s and the frame holds without text and without motion through 54.8 s. The lower third is empty desk.

55.0 to 55.8 s. The split closing composition holds unchanged with no caption: the open-door white car at the airport curb above, the recall card reading The remedy is currently under development with its stamp and the Arriving phone on the desk below. Nothing moves in these five samples.

56.0 to 56.8 s. Hard cut to a dark credits card that fades up: The Daily Dispatch, a Lone Star flag, Texas AI Docket, Visit the Docket texasaidocket.com, then Sources (Waymo, October 14th; NHTSA recall 26E026; Texas Public Radio, May 10th and 13th), Illustration, Map and Music credit lines. Static once faded in.
57.0 to 57.8 s. The same dark credits card holds unchanged: Lone Star flag, Texas AI Docket, texasaidocket.com, Sources, Illustration, Map and Music lines. No motion.

58.0 to 58.8 s. The dark credits card continues to hold unchanged with the Lone Star flag, Texas AI Docket wordmark, texasaidocket.com and the sources, illustration, map and music credit lines. No motion.
59.0 to 59.8 s. The dark credits card holds unchanged across all five samples: Lone Star flag, Texas AI Docket, texasaidocket.com, and the sources, illustration, map and music credit lines.
60.0 to 60.8 s. The dark credits card holds unchanged across all five samples with the Lone Star flag, Texas AI Docket wordmark, texasaidocket.com and the credit lines.

Final phone frame at 60.967 s (frame 1829): the same dark credits card with the Lone Star flag, Texas AI Docket wordmark, texasaidocket.com, and the sources, illustration, map and music credit lines, unchanged from the preceding hold.
